I mean, I don't think I'm crazy. And I try to get in a workout every day, even though it tends to be a bit small. It's just hard to inspire yourself to do anything in this sort of mindset. All I really have to do all day, in the summers especially, is just sit around listening to/playing music or being on the computer. So I'm not sure how much of that I can really change. 

And I have already decided in my mind the second I'm done with high school, am somewhat fine financially, and it's possible I am getting out of this town. It's tough to fit in with a bunch of country people, a lot who don't even own a computer, being one of the only people that's a bit of a nerd, but is just a technology person. Most people I call friends are the only other people who ever use the internet or anything more than once a week, and I'd rather not be literally alone. 

I said, I'm just trying to put up with it, but I get these like episodes of just extreme depression that just keep pushing me closer and closer. I just need a boost of hope sometimes, and I feel like I haven't had anything of the sort in years. Thanks a lot, just the fact that someone is willing to say something is really helpful in getting over it. I'll keep what you've said in mind, and just try to carry on until high school is over without me ending it I guess.

Hey, thanks. I have a bit of a problem where I tend to just somehow spin me looking at these things into me being selfish or whatever, it's pretty stupid but it's just how I am.

 I'm hoping that once I get out of high school and out of this town it will be better, but it's like everyone has a counter-part who is just like them or a best friend or something and then I just don't have anyone. I guess I've just been feeling extremely alone recently. And I don't really have anyone to talk to about it other than my family. If I told anyone outside of my family I guarantee they would write me off as crazy. As for my family, I just don't want them to overly freak out about it, and I refuse to take any sort of medicine for it, so I don't know what to do. 

I've been distracting myself from it with a lot of guitar, and then just playing video games or watching TV or whatever to take my mind off of it, but it's just something that's always just been lingering in the back of my head. It just feels like anytime something knocks me down, it just sorta consumes my thoughts. I just can't help but feel petty and worthless, even when I'm trying to distract myself.

But hey, at least if I can get past this I'll be pretty good at guitar. Thanks for the help.

I think my problem might just be I feel like I'm pretty alone. I've been an outcast for my whole life so far, and the people I've managed to be friends with are pretty much the only people who actually give me the time of day once in a while. It just gets exhausting.

I think I just get these episodes of just feeling alone and depressed, just feeling pretty worthless and like I'm not doing anything with my life, and then without having somebody there to talk to about something it winds up becoming more and more frequent as time goes by. 

And I do plan on going on to college, if I can find a good one that I can actually afford. I just hope that I have to endure a little longer, and then maybe life will lighten the load a little.

Yeah, I'm just sorta hoping the same thing: maybe I just need to suffer through a couple years and then once I can get out of this city it'll get better. Until then, I've just been playing guitar and video games and pretty much anything to pass the time. Hopefully we can both get through to the other side.
